title: REVISED TARGET FOR CONSTRUCTION OF HOUSES UNDER PMAY-G
body_text:
During the last five financial years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26), a total target of 2.13 crore houses has been allocated to the States/UTs under PMAY-G. Against this, 1.95 crore houses have been sanctioned, and 1.21 crore houses have been constructed. The State/UT-wise details of targets allocated, houses sanctioned, houses constructed and houses under construction are provided in Annexure-I.
During the last five financial years, a total Central share of Rs. 1,31,100.02crore has been released to the States/UTs by the Ministry, while Rs. 2,17,896.40 crore (including both Central and State share) has been spent under the scheme. The State/UT-wise details of Central share released by the Ministry and utilization during the last five financial years by is provided in Annexure-II.
The Ministry of Rural Development is implementing the Pradhan MantriAwaasYojana- Gramin (PMAY-G) w.e.f. 1st April 2016 to provide assistance to eligible rural households for the construction of Pucca houses with basic amenities to achieve the objective of "Housing For All" in rural areas. The scheme seeks to provide assistance for the construction of 4.95 crore houses by 31.03.2029. At present, a target of 4.18 crorehouses has been allocated to the States and UTs, and State/UT wise number is given in Annexure- III.
The release of PMAY-G funds had withheld/delayed in certain cases where serious irregularities in implementation were reported and satisfactory corrective action was not established.
In the case of Odisha, complaints alleging irregularities in the implementation of PMAY-G were verified through inquiries by the State Government and Central Teams deputed by the Ministry. The inquiries revealed deficiencies relating to beneficiary selection, construction quality, inspections, branding of PMAY-G houses and compliance with scheme guidelines. Accordingly, the State Government was directed to take corrective and disciplinary action and submit an Action Taken Report (ATR). Since the ATR initially submitted by the State was not found satisfactory, the release of subsequent instalments of Central assistance was withheld pending satisfactory compliance. The State Government has since taken the required corrective and disciplinary measures and submitted a satisfactory ATR. Accordingly, the release of PMAY-G funds to the State has been resumed.
In the case of West Bengal, following the allocation of targets from the finalized Awaas+ 2018 survey lists in November 2022, complaints regarding irregularities in the implementation of PMAY-G were received. These complaints were verified through National Level Monitoring (NLM) teams and Senior Officers Teams following which release of Central share of funds was withheld from FY 2022-23 onwards. The ATR submitted by the State is currently under examination.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development informed Lok Sabha that during FY2021-22 to FY2025-26, 2.13 crore houses were targeted under PMAY-G, of which 1.95 crore were sanctioned and 1.21 crore constructed, with Rs. 1,31,100.02 crore Central share released and Rs. 2,17,896.40 crore spent. PMAY-G aims to build 4.95 crore rural houses by 31.03.2029, with 4.18 crore already allocated as targets. Fund releases were withheld for Odisha and West Bengal due to irregularities; Odisha's funds have resumed after satisfactory corrective action, while West Bengal's Action Taken Report remains under examination since FY2022-23.
enrichment.context:
Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G), launched on 1 April 2016, is the flagship rural housing scheme aimed at achieving 'Housing for All' by providing financial assistance to eligible rural households for pucca houses with basic amenities like toilets, LPG connections, and electricity, often converged with other schemes like MGNREGS and Swachh Bharat Mission. It succeeded the erstwhile Indira Awaas Yojana and uses a cost-sharing pattern (typically 60:40 Centre:State for plains, 90:10 for North-Eastern/Himalayan states, and 100% for UTs) with beneficiaries selected via the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) and Awaas+ surveys to ensure targeting of genuinely poor households.

The withholding of funds to Odisha and West Bengal highlights recurring governance challenges in implementing centrally sponsored schemes, including beneficiary selection irregularities, quality control issues, and political friction between State and Union governments over scheme branding and monitoring. West Bengal has previously seen disputes with the Centre over multiple schemes (including MGNREGS) involving fund suspension over alleged irregularities, making this an ongoing point of Centre-State fiscal federalism tension. The case also underscores the role of National Level Monitoring (NLM) teams and Action Taken Reports (ATRs) as accountability mechanisms in scheme implementation, relevant to India's cooperative federalism and public administration frameworks.

prelims_questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) aims to provide assistance for construction of how many houses by 31.03.2029, as per its current target?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, PMAY-G seeks to provide assistance for the construction of 4.95 crore houses by 31.03.2029, of which 4.18 crore has currently been allocated as targets to States/UTs.

prelims_questions.question: Which Ministry implements the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) scheme?
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that PMAY-G is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development with effect from 1 April 2016.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the objectives and implementation mechanism of the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G). Examine the governance challenges, such as fund withholding due to irregularities in states like Odisha and West Bengal, and suggest measures to strengthen accountability in centrally sponsored schemes.

Centrally sponsored schemes often face implementation bottlenecks due to Centre-State friction over monitoring and fund releases. Analyze this issue with reference to rural housing schemes and suggest institutional reforms to improve cooperative federalism in welfare delivery.
